title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The previous pages set up the following situation. A functor F : (sSet)^op -> B, with B additive and complete, that turns colimits of simplicial sets into limits is determined by a complex K. in B (prop. 2), via F(X.) ~ Hom(C.(X.), K.). Here C.(X.) is the chain complex of X., and Hom is the degree-0 cycles Z^0 of the bicomplex Hom^{ij} = Hom(C_i, K_j). The object Hom(A, M) in B, for A an abelian group and M in B, is the cotensor defined by Hom_B(N, Hom(A,M)) = Hom_Ab(A, Hom_B(N,M)); completeness of B makes it exist.

(1) Top of the page, k-linear case. If B is k-linear (a ring map k -> End(id_B)), it suffices to know C_k.(X.) = C.(X.) (x)_Z k. One has F(X.) ~ Hom_k(C_{.k}, K.) = Z^0 of the bicomplex Hom_k(C_{i,k}, K_j). Here Hom_k(A, M), for A a k-module, is the k-linear cotensor: Hom_B(N, Hom_k(A,M)) = Hom_k(A, Hom_B(N,M)). This is the standard enriched cotensor formula.

(2) Universal example. Among all colimit-to-limit functors from sSet^op into additive complete categories there is a universal one: F_0 : sSet^op -> B_0 = (Ab.)^op, X |-> C.(X), with chain complexes regarded contravariantly. Prop. 3: B_0 is additive with lim. For every such B, composition phi |-> phi o F_0 gives an equivalence Hom_lim(B_0, B) ~ Hom_lim(sSet^op, B), and the latter is ~ complexes in B by prop. 2.

(3) Dold-Puppe variant (marginal note). Replace chain complexes by simplicial abelian groups, (Ab_*)^op ~ (Delta^_ab)^op, and C.(X) by the free simplicial abelian group Z(X.). The statement then becomes Hom^!(Delta^_ab^op, B) ~ Hom^!(Delta^^op, B). Dualizing (done on the next page), it says the following for an arbitrary small category Delta. The abelianization functor Delta^ -> Delta^_ab = Fun(Delta^op, Ab), X |-> Z^(X), is the universal colimit-preserving functor from the presheaf category into additive cocomplete categories. Equivalently, Fun(Delta^op, Ab) is the free additive cocompletion of Delta: colimit-preserving functors out of it into a cocomplete additive A correspond to functors Delta -> A.

The next page proves this via adjoints and representability. It then specializes to Delta = simplex category: n |-> Z(Delta^n) is the universal cosimplicial object in additive cocomplete categories, which Grothendieck labels a corollary 'of Dold-Puppe' type. Purpose: to reduce the construction of cohomology-type functors on simplicial sets (e.g. a divided-power de Rham functor, given by a cosimplicial or complex object K.) to the knowledge of a single complex K. in B.
errors: No substantive errors. As written in chain-complex form, Prop. 3 tacitly needs the Dold-Kan equivalence (Ab_* ~ nonnegative chain complexes); Grothendieck himself switches to the simplicial-abelian form to make the statement clean.

The relevant condition is that F sends colimits in sSet to limits in B (i.e. commutes with lim as a functor on sSet^op). The notation 'commutant aux lim' oscillates between lim-arrows, so one must read it with the opposite category in mind.
Hom(A,M) is written once with the composition order reversed in the transcription; the image is consistent with the standard cotensor formula.

ideas.what: Representation of a colimit-to-limit functor F: sSet^op -> B as Z^0 of the bicomplex Hom(C.(X), K.), using the cotensor Hom(A,M) of B over Ab, and its k-linear version using C.(X) (x) k
ideas.modern_name: Weighted limit / end formula; cotensoring of a complete additive (k-linear) category over Ab (k-Mod); Kan extension along Yoneda
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan (1958, adjoint functors); enriched version Kelly (1982), Day, Street
ideas.where_published: Non-additive analogue in SGA4 Exp. I (extension of functors from C to C^ commuting with colimits)

ideas.what: Universal property of abelianization: Fun(Delta^op, Ab) with X -> Z^(X) is the universal colimit-preserving functor from presheaves on a small category Delta to additive cocomplete categories
ideas.modern_name: Free additive (Ab-enriched) cocompletion; Ab-presheaves on Z[Delta]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly 'Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory' (1982) and earlier folklore; Freyd/Mitchell for the additive Yoneda
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA4 Exp. I; similar universal-property thinking reappears in Pursuing Stacks (1983)

ideas.what: Corollary: the cosimplicial simplicial abelian group n |-> Z(Delta^n) is universal among cosimplicial objects in additive cocomplete categories (Dold-Puppe)
ideas.modern_name: Dold-Kan / Dold-Puppe correspondence via universal cosimplicial object; Yoneda extension (realization/nerve adjunction)

missed.claim: The page frames cohomology-like functors on simplicial sets, such as the divided-power de Rham construction that is the subject of the notes, as colimit-to-limit functors classified by one cosimplicial/complex object via a universal property. This anticipates the later systematic use of the 'cosimplicial model' approach (Sullivan-type polynomial forms, Dold-Kan realization) as categorical universality. It is a viewpoint, not a new result; all statements are standard.
missed.quote: il y en a une "universelle", dont toutes les autres sont "spécialisations"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck working with free additive cocompletions in 1975-76, before Kelly's book, in the service of crystalline/de Rham questions.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean but standard category theory: the Kan-extension universal property of Ab-presheaves and Dold-Kan. It is of interest only as a datable glimpse of how Grothendieck set up the divided-power de Rham complex; there is no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'C. Weyl [?]' is most likely '$C_\cdot \otimes_{\mathbb Z} k$': 'Alors la connaissance de $C_{k\cdot}=C_{k\cdot}(X_\cdot)=C_\cdot\otimes_{\mathbb Z}k$ est encore suffisante'.
'dans B st. [?] lim' should read 'dans B st[able] par lim' ($\varprojlim$).
The underbrace label reads '$\mathcal{H}om^{ij}_k(C_{\cdot k}, K_\cdot)$', i.e. the bicomplex with $\mathcal{H}om^{ij}=\mathcal{H}om_k(C_{i,k},K_j)$.
The marginal vertical note reads roughly 'Variante pour le complexe/l'énoncé de Dold-Puppe', referring to the simplicial-abelian reformulation.
Category names: '$\mathbb{C}_\cdot$' is just the chain complex $C_\cdot$, not a blackboard C.
